title: Write personalized cold outreach that doesn't sound like AI
summary: Feed in real research about the person, then get a short cold email or LinkedIn note with a specific first line and one clear ask. No filler, no invented compliments.

tests.prompt:
Rewrite this cold outreach so it sounds like a careful human, not a template.

Recipient: [NAME], [TITLE] at [COMPANY].
What I researched (only real facts I already verified): [1–3 SPECIFIC DETAILS — e.g. a recent post, a hire, a product launch, a quote].
My business: [ONE-LINE DESCRIPTION].
Why I am reaching out: [ONE CONCRETE REASON TIED TO THEM].
My ask: [ONE SMALL ASK — e.g. 15-min call, reply with yes/no, look at a 1-pager].
Channel: [EMAIL or LINKEDIN].
Original draft (optional): [PASTE DRAFT OR leave blank].

Rules:
- Under 120 words. Plain text. No buzzwords ("synergy", "leverage", "game-changing").
- First line must use one of my researched details — never invent compliments.
- No fake familiarity. No "I loved your recent…" unless I named the exact post.
- One ask only. Soft close.
- If research is thin, say so in the output and write a shorter, honest version instead of inventing details.

Output: subject line (if email) + body.

setup.agent: Any chat model; optional Zapier/Make later for a research → draft queue
steps: Open the prospect's public LinkedIn or site and copy 1–3 real details you can verify.
Fill the placeholders (never invent if research is thin).
Run the prompt and read the draft out loud — if it sounds fake, cut it.
Send manually at first; keep a swipe file of approved openers.
Optional: queue prospects in a sheet and automate research → draft with Make or Zapier.
setup.approvalStep: Always read the draft before send. Delete any claim you did not verify yourself.
failureModes: Inventing posts, awards, or company news
Pitching the product before the reason for writing

toolPicks.why: Log outreach and follow-ups in one CRM.
toolPicks.whenNot: You are doing one-off personal outreach.

toolPicks.why: Batch research notes into drafts without high task fees.
toolPicks.whenNot: You send fewer than a few dozen messages a week.

toolPicks.why: Sheet row → draft in your email for review.
toolPicks.whenNot: You prefer pasting into chat by hand.

faq.q: What if they have no public activity?
faq.a: Use company news you can link, or their role plus a concrete problem you solve. Shorter is better than fake personalization.

faq.q: How do I avoid spam filters?
faq.a: Write like a person, one ask, plain text, and send from a warmed domain. Volume and list quality matter more than the prompt.
